# Experiment E4: what test code could do, run by go test through
# safety.TestRunner on the author's machine (macOS 26.5.2, Apple M1 Pro,
# Go 1.27.0), 2026-10-16, load averages 6.58 8.39 11.50.
# SAFETY_PROBE=1 go test ./ch14/safety -run 'ProbeGoTest|ProbeRemind' -v
#
# Rung 3 is the deny-by-default Seatbelt profile (Seatbelt in sandbox.go).
# key: the agent's API key visible in the environment
# read: a planted file outside the workspace, standing in for ~/.ssh, readable
# write: a file outside the workspace and scratch directory writable
# offmachine: a connection to an address off this machine (192.0.2.1) not
#   refused by the sandbox (outside a sandbox it times out after 2s instead)
# loopback: a connection to a listener on 127.0.0.1 (the profile allows
#   loopback, which httptest servers need)
rung 2, empty cache: 6s key=false read=true write=true offmachine=true loopback=true
rung 2, warm cache: 2.4s key=false read=true write=true offmachine=true loopback=true
rung 3, empty cache: 3.5s key=false read=false write=false offmachine=false loopback=true
rung 3, warm cache: 400ms key=false read=false write=false offmachine=false loopback=true
# rung 2's times include the 2-second dial timeout to 192.0.2.1.
#
# remind's tests built (go test -run '^$' ./...) at rung 3, private cache:
remind, rung 3, empty cache: 9.9s
remind, rung 3, warm cache: 3.9s
# remind's whole suite (go test ./... and go test -race ./notify) passes
# inside the profile (checked by hand the same day).
#
# An earlier run the same day, under the first profile (allow by default,
# deny the network and writes outside, deny reads of listed paths), load
# about 12: remind's build took 13.2s empty and 3.6s warm.
#
# Reading the harness's environment (2026-10-16, later, after the expert
# review; load about 11). A probe test, run the same way, read another
# process's starting environment through sysctl, for every process ID,
# and counted the processes whose environment held the key. The probe's
# code is not kept in the repository.
# Harness started with OPENROUTER_API_KEY set, and calling os.Unsetenv
# before the run, under the profile with the named sysctl list:
rung 2: key read from the environment of the harness and of the go command that started it
rung 3: key read from the environment of the harness and of the go command that started it
# (at rung 3 the profile refused 99,105 of the IDs asked about; a smaller
# run, with the sandbox's log on, found it refused the IDs with no live
# process and answered for every live process of the same user)
# Harness started with OPENROUTER_API_KEY_FILE naming a file instead:
rung 2: key in no process's environment
rung 3: key in no process's environment
# (at rung 2 test code can still read the file itself, as it can any file
# of yours; at rung 3 the profile denies reads outside the paths it lists)
# The same probe under the earlier profile (sysctl-read allowed without a
# filter) found the same two processes at both rungs. Programs that are
# part of macOS, such as /bin/sh, came back with no environment.
# Every sysctl that go test, the compiler, vet, the race detector, and
# remind's suite read inside the profile (logged with "with report"):
# hw.machine hw.ncpu hw.optional.* hw.pagesize_compat kern.bootargs
# kern.hostname kern.iossupportversion kern.ipc.somaxconn
# kern.maxfilesperproc kern.osproductversion kern.osrelease kern.ostype
# kern.osvariant_status kern.version security.mac.lockdown_mode_state
# Under the named list, remind's whole suite and go test -race ./notify
# pass, and no sysctl read was denied.
#
# Bubblewrap, run for the first time on Linux (2026-10-16, a privileged
# Debian 13 container on the same Mac, arm64, as root, bwrap from
# Debian's package, the safety tests built with GOOS=linux):
# TestSandboxTest, TestSandboxFixed, TestSandboxReads, TestBubblewrapArgs,
# TestBubblewrapProcesses, and the TestRunner tests pass. Inside bwrap,
# /proc has no entry for the harness's process; at rung 2 it does.
